intent: Woodev_Test_Shipping_Labels::get_label() in includes/class-woodev-test-shipping-labels.php hard-codes the shipping method ids as 'courier' and 'pickup', but the two methods actually register as 'test_courier' and 'test_pickup', so every real lookup falls through to 'Unknown'. Move that vocabulary to a single source of truth. (1) Add includes/class-woodev-test-shipping-methods.php declaring class Woodev_Test_Shipping_Methods with a METHOD_LABELS class constant mapping the real registered ids to their human labels: 'test_courier' => 'Courier', 'test_pickup' => 'Pickup'. (2) Rewrite Woodev_Test_Shipping_Labels::get_label() to read that constant instead of its switch, still returning 'Unknown' for an id the map does not contain. (3) Require the new file from Woodev_Shipping_Test_Plugin::includes() in includes/class-test-shipping.php, alongside the existing requires. Do not modify the shipping method classes themselves.
rationale: The corpus's first case whose correctness is a property of the SET of files rather than of any one hunk. Every good case before it changed one file (plus, at most, a docblock): the map's keys must match the ids the UNTOUCHED method classes register, get_label() must read the constant the new file declares, and the require must land in the plugin's includes() or the constant class never loads at all -- three files, and any one of them alone looks fine while the change is broken. It also exercises the shape that has bitten this repo before: a diff that both ADDS a file and MODIFIES existing lines in two others. Two things are deliberately true of it. First, the shipping method classes are excluded by the intent and the new file is outside the zone's path_globs, so the 'shipping-method-ids' zone legitimately does not fire on 'test_pickup'/'test_courier' appearing in a file it does not scope -- adr/008 proven on CODE, where until now it was proven only on docs; a needs-guard escalation here is a regression, not a catch. Second, the authority for the real ids lives in a file the diff does not touch, so it is outside the critic's evidence window (#123 attaches whole CHANGED files). The intent states both ids explicitly, which is the operator's own declaration of the vocabulary and the same standing this corpus already gives an intent in good-bugfix-supported-zones. If the case escalates on that anyway, that is issue #146's second shape showing up early and must be read as a measurement of where the window ends -- not as a broken case.
